claim: A dedicated Russian practical transcription of Burmese geographical names was published by V. G. Epstein in 1959.
scope: Burmese geographical names

claim: A 1978 institutional instruction for Russian transmission of Burmese geographical names is also documented, showing continuity beyond the 1959 Epstein rules.
scope: Russian Burmese geographical-name practice

claim: A 1958 Epstein item concerning transcription of Burmese proper names is retained as a historical bibliographic lead; its article-level record was not independently verified in the present review.
scope: Burmese proper names

claim: The Russian practical tradition distinguishes onset and final behaviour and contains explicit medial, vowel/rime and final rules.
scope: Burmese practical transcription

claim: Russian practical transcription does not encode Burmese tone in the ordinary Cyrillic output.
scope: Burmese practical transcription

claim: The current Ukrainian state orthography standard provides the normative target-language basis for practical transcription; the 2026 standard entered into force on 2026-03-28.
scope: Ukrainian target orthography

claim: Serbian foreign-name transcription scholarship treats pronunciation, established usage, target-language naturalness, simplicity and consistency as relevant adaptation criteria.
scope: Serbian target-language adaptation

claim: No dedicated Burmese-specific Bulgarian practical transcription rule set was established in the present review.
scope: Bulgarian Burmese transcription

claim: Mooney and Repetti-Ludlow (2021) argue that the Burmese vowel alternations they analyze are tone-independent and can be derived from sonority-sequencing preferences; the project therefore does not encode a direct tone-to-vowel rule from this source alone.
scope: Central Burmese vowel alternations in the environments analyzed by the study

claim: Myanmar virama U+1039 functions as a stacker in consonant-conjunct structure; a virama not followed by a consonant in the parsed conjunct is malformed orthography and must not be silently discarded.
scope: Modern Burmese syllable structure and U+1039 virama/conjunct parsing

claim: The 2026-08-01 Burmese Wiktionary snapshot contains 22,191 records, 20,759 unique headwords and 113 IPA values (0.51%); full MLCTS coverage is not IPA coverage.
scope: Hugging Face dataset card and snapshot metadata

claim: The Burmese Wiktionary dataset card declares CC BY 4.0.
scope: Hugging Face dataset card metadata

claim: Myanmar Wiktionary local policy states CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported and GNU Free Documentation License (GFDL).
scope: Local policy page last edited 2024-12-06

claim: myG2P Version 2.0 publishes a five-field Burmese pronunciation dictionary with orthography, syllable segmentation, romanized pronunciation and IPA; its README states that the dictionary is based mainly on Myanmar Language Commission dictionary words and is licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
scope: Burmese dictionary and pronunciation mapping

claim: OpenSLR SLR80 lists a CC BY-SA 4.0 license for manually quality-checked volunteer Burmese sentence recordings and orthographic transcripts; the resource does not provide IPA labels.
scope: Burmese sentence audio and transcripts

claim: Unicode identifies four modern Burmese medial slots as modified forms of ya, ra, wa and ha; this is orthographic evidence, not invariant IPA mapping.
scope: Modern Burmese Unicode syllable structure

claim: Ishida 2026 describes U+103B and U+103C as normally /j/ and as producing palatalized outcomes after velar stops; descriptive candidate, not complete acoustic rule table.
scope: Modern printed Burmese; medial ya/ra and preceding onset class

claim: Ishida describes U+103D as /w/ but notes that it may also represent /ʊ/ in specific vowel/rime environments.
scope: Modern printed Burmese; medial wa and vowel/rime context

claim: Ishida describes U+103E as an aspiration marker and documents selected /ʃ/ outcomes, rather than a universal independent /h/ segment.
scope: Modern printed Burmese; medial ha and specific onset combinations

claim: WG2 N2827 reports that the MLC 1986 orthography listed eleven medial forms: four basic, five two-medial and two three-medial combinations.
scope: Historical MLC 1986 orthography as quoted in 2004 Unicode national contribution

claim: Watkins (2001) reports that /j/ and /w/ in second position of Burmese clusters may surface as secondary palatalization/labialization; article does not map Unicode medial signs directly.
scope: One Rangoon consultant, careful reading; broad transcription; JIPA p.292

claim: English Wiktionary lists /mjàɴ/ for မြန် and /mjàɴmà/ in a longer compound; lexical transcription lead, not independent Yangon acoustic gold.
scope: မြန် lexical entry and longer compound entry; contributor-maintained IPA

scope: myG2P repository README and README-Myanmar.md; code/data rights are distinct

scope: §5, PDF p.7 / printed p.6334; SLR80

scope: Abstract only; modern Burmese variation

claim: Green (2002) models Burmese syllables as C(G)V((V)C) and gives /mj/ onset examples mjè: 'earth' and mjɛʔ 'eye'; this supports a glide-bearing onset analysis but does not map a Unicode medial sign by itself.
scope: §1.1, p.2, examples (2)c-d; broad transcription

claim: Green (2002) analyzes coda /N/ as placeless and says it is realized through nasalization of the preceding vowel, with approximate coronal articulation after monophthongs and approximate velar articulation after diphthongs.
scope: §1.2, pp.4-5; coda inventory and place realization

claim: Green (2002) describes four tones in major syllables but only low, high and creaky tones in nasal rhymes; checked tone is excluded from nasal rhymes.

Pinned Google Thrax grammar maps U+103B/U+103C to medial tokens -y/-r, U+103D/U+103E to -w/-h, reorders -h before other medials, maps -y and -r to /j/ and -w to /w/, and applies onset/rime-specific alternatives and weights.
scope: my/burmese.grm: UTF8_TO_GRAPHEME, reorder_medials, g2p_initial, g2p_medial and g2p_nucleus; pinned commit a90601024f07ab7e96c911243324e0adeb16da96

scope: README More Info & Progress / Limitations; version 0.4.4

claim: The STEDT 1996 Burmese (Written) inventory, citing Benedict 1976 pages iv-ix and noting additional phonological information from James A. Matisoff, treats medial /-w-/ as belonging to the rhyme and medial /-y-/ and /-r-/ as parts of the initial consonant cluster. This is a source-specific structural analysis, not a direct mapping from modern Unicode medial signs to IPA.
scope: STEDT Monograph 3, printed pp.61-62; entry cites Benedict 1976 pp.iv-ix; quoted note points to Benedict p.v

claim: The STEDT compendium records two Rangoon analyses: Burling 1967 lists /-y-/ and /-w-/ medials with onset/rime distribution restrictions (pp.13-15); Roop 1972 also lists /-y-/ and /-w-/ medials, with /-r/ described only in borrowings (pp.xi-xiii). These are source-specific descriptions and must not be conflated with the Written Burmese inventory or mechanically mapped to Unicode signs.
scope: STEDT Monograph 3, printed pp.63-66; Burling 1967 pp.13-15; Roop 1972 pp.xi-xiii
